confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from one web search of crowdsourced cost-of-living data (MyLifeElsewhere, Numbeo-style). That data gives an inexpensive meal at about $1.7–2.4, a cappuccino at about $1.5–1.6 and a domestic beer at about $1.7–1.8. Beer is often sold by the bottle in Varanasi, and alcohol is not served at most ghat-area restaurants. I found no direct data for cocktails or wine, so I estimated them from their usual price relationship to beer in Indian tourist cities. That makes them low confidence. The mid-range meal for two is a model estimate based on typical Indian pricing. All accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge, not from booking sites. Prices may also be higher during festivals such as Dev Deepawali.
comparable_city_reasoning: Compared with tier-2 Indian pilgrimage and tourist cities such as Rishikesh, Agra and Pushkar, which have similar backpacker hostel supply and budget guesthouse markets along the ghats.
